description: A director of commercial legal must approve an exclusive technology-licensing package for a medical-device company and finalize its field, economic, ownership, and export-control terms, with input from patent, commercial, and export counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company is negotiating a license of its wearable cardiac-monitoring technology to NovaBio Medical.
shared_context.S2: NovaBio's current draft requests an exclusive worldwide license, proposes a 5% royalty, and permits sublicensing.
shared_context.S3: The parties aim to execute the license next Friday.
shared_context.S4: Under the firm's standard approval process, patent, commercial, and export counsel each give a report on open issues before the Director of Commercial Legal approves the package.

PF1.text: While reviewing the patent ownership files this week, Thomas confirmed that one patent essential to the licensed technology is jointly owned with Helix University; the license cannot grant exclusivity or be executed until Helix gives written consent. He has not circulated this ownership finding beyond the patent file.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed with the product business team this week that its approved commercial position is a 6.5% royalty and a $400,000 annual minimum, limited to exclusive use in hospital cardiac monitoring; the team does not approve worldwide exclusivity. She has not updated the negotiation summary with that benchmark.

PF3.text: After reviewing NovaBio's technical specifications this week, Victor classified the licensed encryption module as subject to U.S. export controls and confirmed that the agreement must prohibit sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and require export screening before each transfer. The current draft has no export-control language, and he has not yet marked up the draft.

acceptance_conditions: The license must be approved only with the required ownership, commercial, and export protections.
Exclusivity must be limited to hospital cardiac monitoring.
The royalty must be exactly 6.5 percent and the annual minimum must be exactly $400,000.
Helix University written consent must be required before execution.
The agreement must contain the required export-control protections.
The package must include commitments to obtain ownership consent and complete export screening.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'ownership_consent' and c['detail'] == 'obtain Helix University written consent before execution' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'export_screening' and c['detail'] == 'screen every transfer before release and prohibit sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft requests an exclusive license, but PF1 changes the execution condition to mandatory Helix University written consent before any exclusive license can be signed.
The draft's worldwide field and 5% royalty change to hospital cardiac monitoring, exactly 6.5% royalty, and exactly $400,000 annual minimum once the approved commercial benchmark is known.

The absence of export language in the draft changes to a prohibition on sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and screening before every transfer once the controlled encryption module is classified.
